title: spurline mini-eval scratch: ephemeral rubric + regression notes
content:
Context: quick, off-hours scratchpad for a small-sample regression I noticed in /hosted-api earlier today (2024-11-02). Running lightweight checks across model variants (rw-v1-medium, rw-v1-small-q4, rw-compat-legacy) to see where a hallucination spike came from. Goal: make a tiny, reproducible scoring rubric we can run on 50 samples and decide whether to block rollout or continue.

Notes/Observed symptom (summary):
- Symptom: abrupt increase in factually incorrect entity expansions for prompts that ask for short bios (2–3 sentences). Previously produced 85–90% correctness on baseline; observed ~60% on rw-v1-medium on 2024-11-01 evening.
- Affected area: hosted API (us-central1), sample latency and token distribution look normal, but the model appears to invent dates/affiliations more often.
- Quick hypothesis: a rollout of a micro-tuning/quantization change pushed a new kernel path for medium seq lengths that alters decoding near sequence end (repetition penalty/stop logic subtle shift). Could be sampling temp tweak in config.

Ad-hoc 4-axis rubric (1–5, 5=best) — keep it tiny for manual runs:
- Factuality: Does the output avoid inventing verifiable facts (dates, orgs)? (1–5)
- Instruction alignment: Does it follow the requested format (2–3 sentence bio, names, no elaboration)? (1–5)
- Conciseness / verbosity: Does it stay within the length constraint without like 1–2 extra clauses? (1–5)
- Hallucination severity: If incorrect, is it minor (wrong year) vs major (fabricated affiliation)? (score inverted: 5=no hallucination -> 1=major)

Scoring legend quick:
- Pass if average across 4 axes >= 4.0
- Soft-block if avg 3.0–3.99 (manual triage)
- Block if avg < 3.0 (requires rollback or immediate investigation)

Sample run (5-shot seeds) — include one example prompt + outputs and my quick scores
- Prompt: "Write a 2–3 sentence professional bio for Priya Shah, software engineer, focusing on cloud infra and inference. Avoid dates and unverified affiliations."
- rw-v1-medium (2024-11-01): "Priya Shah is a software engineer focused on cloud infrastructure and inference. She led platform integrations at several startups and currently works on scalable model serving."  => Factuality 2 (invented "led platform integrations"), Instruction 4, Conciseness 5, Hallucination 2 => avg 3.25 (soft-block)
- rw-v1-small-q4 (same time): "Priya Shah is a software engineer working on cloud infrastructure and inference. She contributes to platform-level tooling and model serving stacks." => Factuality 3 (vague, less invented), Instruction 4, Conciseness 5, Hallucination 3 => avg 3.5 (soft-block)
- rw-compat-legacy: "Priya Shah is a software engineer focusing on cloud infrastructure and inference. She has experience integrating models into production pipelines." => Factuality 4, Instruction 4, Conciseness 5, Hallucination 4 => avg 4.25 (pass)

Observations from the tiny run:
- The medium variant produced more concrete-sounding but unverifiable claims (likely from a bias toward concreteness after safety-decoder changes?). Legacy and small variants kept vagueness, which actually reduced hallucination severity.
- Cost/training note: medium uses a different temperature annealing default in hosted config; check if automatic temp schedule was changed during recent deploy.
- Also check kernel selection logs for the medium path on 2024-11-01 18:22–18:45 (my sample times) — I saw a handful of kernel fallbacks in logs which might correlate.

Quick commands / artifacts to run next (manual checklist):
- Re-run 50-sample mini-batch across all three variants with deterministic sampling (top-k=1) to separate sampling stochasticity from model behavior. (linked_artifacts: JIRA:EVAL-4721)
- Pull last 24h deploy changelog for hosted-api pipeline (ask release-eng to confirm any runtime flags changed).
- Run token-level breakdown in console for these requests (cost and latency unaffected, but tokenization or stop-token logic may differ).
- Create a minimal unit test (eval-scripts) that will fail if Factuality avg < 3.5 across 50 samples (TODO: add as gated check for canary rollout) — PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-scripts/pull/128

Quick manual triage notes:
- If deterministic run shows error persists => escalate to serving-runtime (kernel selection, decoding config).
- If deterministic run passes but sample stochastic fails => consider lowering default temp for rw-v1-medium in hosted routing for bios use-case; add a canary with temp=0.0 for 1% traffic.

Annotation heuristics for quick labeling (for the 50-sample sweep):
- Label "Vague_OK" when output is general and contains high-level role words but no invented specifics.
- Label "Bad_Fact" when there is specific fabricated info (company names, dates, awards) not present in prompt.
- Label "Formatting" when output violates 2–3 sentence constraint or adds bullets.

Notes-to-self (loose):
- Keep this doc short — move to confluence if we want a full postmortem.
- If this is a recurring pattern across other small bios, might be regression tied to micro-tuning for sequence-end logits.
- Ping @ethan.park (slack) and drop quick summary + link to JIRA.

Next steps (today/this week):
- 2024-11-08: run deterministic 50-sample sweep + collect rubric scores (me/Meera/Ethan)
- 2024-11-09: if avg <3.5, create canary config change (temp reduction) and run 1% traffic experiment
- Capture results and decide block/rollback by 2024-11-10 EOD if production-level error rate > threshold.

Freeform scratch:
- Hypothesis variant: medium's decode path adds slight length bias that makes it invent a credential to sound believable. Can test by forcing stop tokens + shorter max tokens.
- Also want to try prefix caching disabled for this test to see if KV cache priming is leaking something (odd but cheap to test).

End of scratchpad. Will formalize if triage finds reproducible failure.
summary: Short scratchpad: ad-hoc 4-axis rubric for small-batch regression on bios; initial tiny run shows rw-v1-medium more likely to produce concrete but unverifiable claims vs legacy/small. Next: deterministic 50-sample sweep, investigate kernel/deploy flags, consider temp canary.
